note: A priority encoder written with casez - the standard use of the construct. Covers hif-backend#84, fixed by hif-backend 54c9e82: hif2verilog used to regenerate the `casez` as a plain `case` with the `?` bits spelled `z`, so under exact matching every wildcard alternative was unreachable and five of the eight rows fell through to the default. It now emits `casez`. Behavioural because nothing else can see it: both spellings are valid Verilog around the same alternatives, and the regenerated file exits 0 and reparses cleanly either way. The 1000 and 0000 rows need no wildcard and act as controls, so a failure reads as 'the wildcards are gone' rather than as a scrambled encoder. The oracle is unchanged from when it was expected to fail; it went green on the fix alone.
